header:
Date: 2025-12-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Carlos Rivera (Northridge Head of Cloud), Priya Nanda (Northridge CISO), Emily Zhao (Northridge Compliance), Asha Mehta (Northridge Eng)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency and compliance implications for using Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer expressed strict data residency for EU/UK customers, logging restrictions for financial PII, and auditability requirements. Redwood team outlined trade-offs, Private/VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM options, and proposed next steps to share security artifacts and run a technical deep dive.
topics: Logging and token retention policies (no PII in logs, redaction)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Compliance: SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR, HIPAA considerations
Network architecture for Private/VPC and on-prem options
transcript_body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team. quick intro?
[00:10] Carlos Rivera: Hi, Carlos here, head of cloud at Northridge. Priya is our CISO and Emily handles compliance, Asha is engineering.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. today we wanted to understand your residency and compliance constraints and talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private. Maya our SE will jump into the technicals.
[00:27] Maya Patel: hey all, hi. quick note—apologies for any audio artifacts my mic is a little low.
[00:31] Priya Nanda: no problem. to start, high level: we have a requirement that all EU/UK customer data must remain in EU/UK data centers, no replication to US. also financial transaction PII cannot be stored in vendor logs longer than 24 hours and must be redacted.
[00:47] Jordan Lee: understood, thanks. can you clarify \"customer data\" — are we talking full request/response payloads, or tokens/embeddings as well?
[00:55] Emily Zhao: mostly request/response payloads and model inputs that include account numbers, but we also want to control embeddings and any derived features. 
[01:03] Asha Mehta: there's also the audit trail requirement — logs must be available for internal audit, and third party auditors may request them under NDA. we can't have unencrypted logs sitting in shared buckets.
[01:13] Maya Patel: ok. so two axes: physical residency and how logs/tokens are handled. Redwood hosted can be region-restricted to EU for processing but standard hosted keeps some operational logs aggregated across regions for meta-telemetry; that may conflict. for strict isolation we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:30] Priya Nanda: what's the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of data residency and network controls?
[01:35] Maya Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in a region and logical isolation — your tenant's data and models are isolated, and we can limit data to the region, but control plane and some ops telemetry may still be routed through Redwood control plane in the US unless you choose Dedicated with private control options. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you a customer-managed control plane option: you can deploy the control plane in your VPC or on-prem, and logs, model artifacts, and KV caches stay under your network boundary.
[01:56] Carlos Rivera: so Private means we host the control plane? we have a compliance mandate that control plane metadata must remain in EU.
[02:01] Maya Patel: yes, for our Private package we offer a private control plane that you run in your VPC or on-prem. we support integration with your KMS/HSM for key custody and you control storage endpoints.
[02:12] Priya Nanda: KMS/HSM — do you support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and bring-your-own-HSM?
[02:17] Jordan Lee: we support AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault natively, and we have integrations for customer-managed HSMs via PKCS#11. for the Private deployment, keys never leave your HSM if you configure external key custody.
[02:28] Emily Zhao: good. second question — logging. we need assurance that PII and cardholder data is never logged. how do you handle token logging and model input retention?
[02:36] Maya Patel: by default Redwood can be configured not to persist raw request/response payloads for hosted — we retain short-term ephemeral data for routing and debugging but you can opt out. for Dedicated and Private, you control retention windows. we also offer automatic redaction filters that can be applied to known patterns like PANs, SSNs — it's pattern based, not perfect but helps. note transcription might say PANs as pans sometimes in logs.
[02:57] Carlos Rivera: is that redaction done before any logs leave our VPC for Private?
[03:01] Maya Patel: yes, in Private deployments redaction runs inside your environment before any telemetry is sent to Redwood control plane — unless you configure otherwise.
[03:08] Priya Nanda: HIPAA — we have a small business line that needs to be HIPAA compliant. can Redwood be used for PHI?
[03:15] Jordan Lee: Redwood can support HIPAA-ready setups. we have customers who use Private deployments with BAAs. we'll send the legal pack; we do require Private or Dedicated with strict contract terms for PHI in most cases.
[03:27] Asha Mehta: what about subject access requests under GDPR — if a user requests deletion, how do you guarantee deletion from model cache or embeddings?
[03:36] Maya Patel: good question — we treat embeddings and cached KV as data that can be scoped. for Private you manage storage so you can delete; for Dedicated we provide APIs to expire cached keys and delete embeddings; for Hosted we have deletion workflows but you need to be explicit about retention policies. we'll document the exact API calls in the follow-up.
[03:55] Carlos Rivera: regulatory auditors will also want proof of encryption at rest and in transit, and chain of custody for keys. do you provide audit logs that show key usage?
[04:03] Jordan Lee: yes — we can export audit trails and integrate with your SIEM. for Private we can keep audit logs inside your logging stack and still provide hashes to Redwood for cross-checks; we'll send examples.
[04:13] Priya Nanda: network wise, we need to restrict egress to only our monitoring endpoints. can Private deployment work in an air-gapped or restricted egress environment?
[04:21] Maya Patel: Private on-prem can be run air-gapped; some features like Redwood-managed model updates would require planned sync windows. for VPC Private we support strict egress rules and allow model downloads from controlled S3 endpoints.
[04:33] Emily Zhao: any limitations on model variants or quantization when running Private? we use INT8 quantized models for cost.
[04:40] Maya Patel: we support quantized variants in all deployment modes; however some optimized kernels in hosted runtime are tuned for our cloud infra. Private has the full runtime but we may need to validate kernel support for specific GPUs. we'll run a compatibility checklist during the technical deep dive.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: quick interruption — they asked about auditability around prompts, i.e., do you store prompts unencrypted?
[05:02] Maya Patel: prompts can be stored encrypted at rest and keyed by your KMS. in Private the keys are yours; in Dedicated you can integrate KMS. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers.
[05:14] Carlos Rivera: what about logging restrictions — our auditors want evidence that no raw PII is present in aggregated analytics dashboards. how do you separate telemetry and PII?
[05:23] Maya Patel: we separate token-level telemetry from analytics. analytics are computed from aggregated metrics, not raw texts. token counts, latency, error rates are kept but payloads are not surfaced in dashboards. you can opt to disable payload-based debugging.
[05:36] Priya Nanda: competitor question — we've spoken to OpenAI and Anthropic; they mention not storing content and token logging options. why choose Redwood?
[05:44] Jordan Lee: Redwood focuses on production economics and deployment flexibility — if you need strict residency and private control plane we can provide Private and on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed logging. we also provide transparent perf profiles and cost-optimization tooling.
[05:58] Asha Mehta: cost question — do you have baseline pricing for Dedicated versus Private?
[06:03] Jordan Lee: we will send a brief pricing worksheet. Dedicated is committed capacity in a region; Private includes packaging for the private control plane and optionally on-prem support. we'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[06:13] Carlos Rivera: on the data residency side, we have EU customers and regulatory must not move data to US. can you guarantee that backups or failover won't replicate to US?
[06:23] Maya Patel: for Dedicated we can set region lock and replicate only within chosen zones; backups can be configured to residence in the same region. for Private your storage endpoints are within your control so you can guarantee no cross-region replication. we'll include the runbook showing region lock behavior.
[06:39] Priya Nanda: last technical — third party auditors might request logs, we need to redact account numbers but preserve trace ids for correlation. possible?
[06:46] Maya Patel: yes — we support tokenization/redaction that retains a stable hash or trace id while removing the PII string. that's a common pattern we use for audits.
[06:56] Jordan Lee: ok team, sounds like next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO, a Private deployment architecture doc, pricing, and schedule the deep dive. any other questions?
[07:07] Emily Zhao: one little thing — do you have any references in finance?
[07:10] Jordan Lee: yes, we have a short reference list and case studies; we'll include anonymized examples and contact info if you want an intro.
[07:18] Carlos Rivera: perfect. thanks everyone.
[07:21] Jordan Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and proposed times for the deep dive.
[07:25] [Call ends]
